title: AI, Education, and K-12 Digital Equity
published_window: 2026-06 to 2026-07 (search index: 3 months ago; exact date not exposed)
discussion_signal: The post relays national-principal survey findings that AI use rose quickly while integration was lower in more disadvantaged schools, and connects the gap to district capacity, training, guidance, teacher champions, and governance. A comment explicitly distinguishes tool adoption from the harder work of building reasoning and policy scaffolding.
linked_research_question: Whether fast AI adoption in schools is translating into equitable, governed learning practice, or widening gaps through unequal implementation capacity.
limits: Post is a secondary relay of the NBER working paper
LinkedIn commenters are a selected audience
Reported associations do not establish that district capacity causes the full disadvantage gap
